acetaminophen.title: Acetaminophen / paracetamol
acetaminophen.text: Generally kidney-safe at recommended doses. Check combination cold/pain products to prevent duplicate dosing. Liver disease requires separate advice. No numeric CKD or dialysis regimen is curated here.

systemic-nsaid.title: Systemic NSAID safety
systemic-nsaid.text: Systemic NSAIDs can cause AKI and worsen CKD. NKF advises avoidance in CKD, especially eGFR <60; do not self-treat. If a clinician selects one, use an individual risk assessment, the lowest dose and shortest duration. This is a class warning, not a dialysis dosing protocol.

topical-pain.title: Topical pain products
topical-pain.text: Label-directed topical pain products generally have lower kidney risk. Diclofenac gel has less systemic exposure than oral diclofenac. Do not exceed application limits. Lower systemic exposure does not establish safety for every product or patient.

aspirin.title: Distinguish aspirin indications
aspirin.text: Analgesic/high-dose aspirin carries NSAID kidney risks. Do not use this warning to stop prescribed low-dose antiplatelet aspirin; verify the indication and exact product with the treating team.

antacid.title: Antacid ingredients in CKD
antacid.text: Calcium, magnesium, bismuth and aluminium ingredients can accumulate in CKD. Check the exact combination and renal-team advice. NKF advises avoiding aluminium-containing products because of brain toxicity. This does not define prescribed phosphate-binder dosing.

h2.title: H2 blocker accumulation
h2.text: H2 blockers such as cimetidine and nizatidine are renally cleared and may require lower doses or longer intervals. This safety note does not provide a renal regimen; obtain a product-specific recommendation.

ppi.title: OTC proton pump inhibitors
ppi.text: Discuss OTC PPI use with the kidney team. Reassess prolonged treatment and potential kidney/mineral adverse effects. An absence of renal dose reduction does not justify unsupervised long-term use.

phosphate.title: Sodium phosphate bowel preparations
phosphate.text: Oral sodium phosphate bowel preparations can cause kidney injury and should be avoided in CKD. Do not extrapolate an alternative bowel-preparation prescription from this warning.

decongestant.title: Cold remedies and decongestants
decongestant.text: Kidney Care UK advises avoiding decongestant-containing cold remedies, including pseudoephedrine and phenylephrine, especially with hypertension. Check all active ingredients in combination products.

constipation.title: Constipation products
constipation.text: Kidney Care UK lists senna as an option. Bulk-forming ispaghula/psyllium may be unsuitable with fluid restriction. Persistent constipation and PD-related constipation need renal-team advice; no dose is selected here.

diarrhoea.title: Diarrhoea and rehydration
diarrhoea.text: Kidney Care UK lists loperamide as an option for selected minor diarrhoea. Severe illness needs assessment. Use oral rehydration salts only if the treating team recommends them; fluid and electrolyte restrictions matter.

drugs.name: Captopril
drugs.formulation: Oral · UK solution renal table; doses are mg, not mL
drugs.kidneyMetric: CrCl · mL/min/1.73 m² as written in the UK product table
drugs.summary: Renally eliminated and removable by HD. The UK table gives TOTAL daily starting and maximum amounts, not amounts per dose.

tables.indication: UK renal table · TOTAL daily amounts, not per-dose amounts

rows.dose: Initial total 25–50 mg/day; maximum total 150 mg/day
Initial total 25 mg/day; maximum total 100 mg/day
Initial total 12.5 mg/day; maximum total 75 mg/day
Initial total 6.25 mg/day; maximum total 37.5 mg/day

ckd.notes: Select the dosing frequency separately. These maxima are limits, not treatment targets. Preserve the indexed source metric and verify gaps at fractional CrCl boundaries.

ihd.notes: Captopril is removable from adult circulation by HD. An individual dose, session timing and any supplement require an approved renal protocol; the non-dialysis table is not an HD prescription.

crrt.notes: No prescription-specific regimen curated. Do not extrapolate from IHD or CKD.

pd.notes: The US label states that PD does not effectively remove captopril. This does not establish a PD maintenance dose.

sled.notes: No prescription-specific regimen curated. Do not extrapolate from IHD or CKD.

drugs.considerations: Individualise the divided-dose schedule and titrate slowly; monitor BP, potassium and renal function. Confirm the local formulation/concentration. ACE inhibitors can cause membrane-associated anaphylactoid reactions; check the dialysis membrane and full label. Do not infer a post-HD supplemental dose from the removal statement.
drugs.completeness: Selected adult renal starting/maximum total daily amounts and PK only. The renal table does not define the frequency or an RRT regimen. Full indication, interaction and contraindication review is required.
drugs.jurisdiction: UK oral-solution renal table; US tablet label supports PK/removal statements. Local product instructions must be checked.

halfLife.context: Unchanged parent drug. Half-life of total captopril/disulfide material is a different measure.

volumeOfDistribution.context: Steady-state Vss after IV dosing in five healthy subjects; central Vd 0.2 L/kg and terminal-phase Vd 2 L/kg are different measures.

ihd.context: Adult circulation. The checked label does not supply a universal removal percentage.

crrt.context: Modality-specific removal data have not been curated.

sled.context: Modality-specific removal data have not been curated.

pharmacokinetics.notes: Renal impairment causes accumulation. UKKA ESRF half-life 21–32 h is a reference-table value; the table does not specify free parent versus total captopril/disulfide material. Do not calculate a dose ratio from the two half-lives.

rows.context: At end of each HD treatment
rows.dose: 0.5 micrograms/kg IV bolus using target dry body weight

drugs.name: Sodium zirconium cyclosilicate
drugs.summary: The chronic-HD schedule differs from non-dialysis correction dosing.

rows.dose: 10 g PO three times daily for up to 48 h
Usually 10 g daily; titrate per potassium and full label
5 g PO once daily on NON-dialysis days only

ihd.notes: Consider 10 g initial dose on non-dialysis days if K >6.5 mEq/L; this does not replace emergency management. Reassess pre-HD potassium after the long interval.

drugs.considerations: Not an emergency treatment for life-threatening hyperkalaemia. Monitor potassium and oedema/sodium burden. Other oral medicines generally require ≥2 h separation; check label exceptions.
